rv.q: It's a riveting and unflinching look back at the painful and exhilarating business of growing up with a powerful friendship to bolster you through it.
A comic drama like this should run 80 or 90 minutes with no intermission, so minimizing the costume changes and trimming the script, especially in the second act, would help.

cn.t: Critics praise this comic coming-of-age story for its sharp exploration of teenage friendship and identity, with compelling performances capturing the hormones, solidarity, and bumpy realities of being 13-year-old girls in 1980s Chicago.
